question: A poorly nourished child living in a crowded area comes down with frequent infections. Which factor is most responsible for lowering this child's defenses?

question: What is the main purpose of a soft diet?

question: What happens inside the brain when there is a severe shortage of thiamine?

question: Which conflict management strategy involves both sides working together to find a solution that satisfies everyone?

question: How does taking time to build good rapport with a patient help your qualitative interview?

question: When should the nurse stop the repeating cycles of fluid instillation and drainage during a gastric lavage?

question: How do transdermal patches differ from ordinary skin creams?

options.C: Transdermal patches are designed for systemic absorption
options.D: Standard creams always enter the bloodstream faster than patches

question: What is behaviorism primarily focused on?

question: Which mineral does the body need to make thyroid hormones?

question: What is the main thing you do during the evaluation phase of the nursing process?

question: Why is regular aerobic exercise considered beneficial for a patient's lipid profile?

question: You are feeding a patient who looks very tired and worn out. What is the safest way to handle their meal?

options.A: Allowing frequent rest periods and offering smaller, more frequent meals

options.C: Mixing all the food together so it is easier to swallow quickly
options.D: Feeding the remaining food much faster to finish on time

explanation: Tired muscles make swallowing mistakes easy. Pacing the meal and serving smaller portions keeps your patient safe and energized. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T7#GNS112_U5_T7_h4)

question: A patient feels very embarrassed and down about sexual changes after prostate surgery. How should you respond as a nurse?

options.A: Acknowledge his feelings and offer a supportive, nonjudgmental space to discuss concerns
options.B: Tell him that sexual function is entirely unimportant compared to curing his urinary obstruction
options.C: Advise him to immediately stop taking all prescribed postoperative medications
options.D: Assure him that normal function always returns within twenty-four hours

explanation: Being heard and accepted with empathy helps patients cope with sensitive body-image and emotional challenges after major surgery. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T9#GNS311_U1_T9_h6)

question: Which vaccine is routinely administered to pregnant women during antenatal care visits to prevent a specific neonatal infection?

options.A: Tetanus toxoid
options.B: Measles vaccine

options.D: Bacille Calmette-Guérin

question: What should you do immediately after a drain is successfully pulled out from a surgical wound?

options.A: Ask the patient to stand up and walk around the room

options.C: Wash the open tract thoroughly with harsh antiseptic soap

question: Why do doctors usually choose levothyroxine over other options for thyroid replacement?

options.A: It contains both active and inactive hormones in variable amounts
options.B: It has a predictable potency and smooth onset of action
options.C: It is derived directly from animal thyroid glands
options.D: It acts much faster than synthetic triiodothyronine

explanation: Levothyroxine is lab-made and gives a steady, reliable daily dose. No nasty surprises or wild hormone spikes! [learn more](GNS223_U7_T2#GNS223_U7_T2_h2)

question: Why is an individualized care plan so important in rehabilitation?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to document patient progress.

options.C: Insurance companies refuse to pay for care plans that mention physical therapy.
options.D: Standardized care plans are illegal in specialized hospital settings.

explanation: Exactly! No two patients are alike, even with the same diagnosis. Their care must fit their unique lifestyle, support system, and personal goals. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T10#GNS324_U5_T10_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of an advanced healthcare directive?

options.A: To permit nurses to alter medical prescriptions independently
options.B: To guarantee financial compensation for hospital admission
options.C: To guide medical treatment choices before a patient loses the ability to decide
options.D: To protect the hospital from paying taxes on equipment

explanation: You nailed it! Advanced directives let people state their medical wishes ahead of time just in case they can't speak later. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is the medical term for the patchy, purplish skin color that appears on the hands and feet when circulation slows down?

options.A: Cyanosis
options.B: Jaundice
options.C: Mottling
options.D: Erythema

explanation: Mottling happens when blood flow slows way down, causing blood to pool in the hands and feet with a purplish, blotchy pattern. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS221_U4_T4#GNS221_U4_T4_h2)

question: How can you best help a patient with a tracheostomy tube who temporarily cannot speak?

options.A: Temporarily remove parts of the tube
options.B: Provide writing pads or communication boards
options.C: Tell them to whisper to keep their voice strong
options.D: Ask only yes-or-no questions for head nods

explanation: Spot on! Alternative tools like writing boards let patients express themselves clearly without straining or irritating their airway. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T5#GNS213_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the main reason we advise pregnant women to eat small, frequent meals?

options.A: To eliminate the need for drinking water entirely
options.B: To prevent the stomach from becoming overly full and distended
options.C: To speed up the transit time of food through the large intestine
options.D: To increase total daily calorie consumption by fifty percent

question: What is the primary reason nursing pharmacology education became much more rigorous over the past century?

options.A: Patients no longer wanted to take natural remedies.
options.B: Modern medications became significantly more potent and complex, increasing risks.
options.C: Physicians stopped prescribing medications altogether.
options.D: Nurses took over the responsibility of manufacturing hospital drugs.

explanation: As drugs became more powerful, the potential for dangerous side effects and interactions grew, requiring nurses to possess advanced pharmacological knowledge to protect patients. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why are older adult patients at a higher risk for medication mix-ups during home care?

options.A: Their bodies cannot process basic tap water safely
options.B: They frequently take multiple medications at the same time
options.C: They always refuse to take any form of pill or liquid
options.D: Doctors rarely prescribe standard adult doses to seniors

explanation: Taking many drugs at once (polypharmacy) increases the chance of drug interactions, side effects, and confusion. You'll see this often in community health! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h7)

question: What is the main focus of a national nursing organization like NANNM?

options.A: Country-specific labor laws and domestic health policies
options.B: Directing medical research for pharmaceutical corporations
options.C: Global monetary funds for hospital construction worldwide
options.D: Setting international travel guidelines for nurse migration

explanation: National bodies focus right at home—handling local working conditions, salaries, and health policies that directly affect nurses in our country. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T5#GNS112_U1_T5_h3)

question: How does breastfeeding help a mother's body immediately after delivery?

options.A: It prevents all future menstrual cycles permanently

options.C: It repairs perineal tears without surgical intervention
options.D: It stimulates uterine contractions to reduce postpartum bleeding

question: What is the main difference between acute and chronic pain?

options.A: Acute pain is tied to recent tissue injury and resolves with healing, while chronic pain lasts long past the normal healing period.
options.B: Acute pain can be measured with scales, but chronic pain cannot be measured.
options.C: Acute pain requires no medical treatment, whereas chronic pain requires surgery.
options.D: Acute pain only affects internal organs, while chronic pain only affects the skin and muscles.

explanation: Think of acute pain as a sudden alarm bell that stops when healing happens, while chronic pain sticks around long after the injury has healed. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T5#GNS321_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why does the pancreas send bicarbonate along with its digestive enzymes?

options.A: To break down complex proteins into simple amino acids
options.B: To protect the liver from viral infections
options.C: To stimulate the gallbladder to release stored bile
options.D: To neutralize stomach acid and create the right pH for enzymes

question: What is the best nursing response when a patient believes their blood disorder is caused entirely by spiritual forces?

options.A: Report the family to hospital security for refusing modern medicine

options.C: Respect their beliefs while gently providing education on the medical condition
options.D: Scold the patient and family for holding unscientific ideas

explanation: Respect builds trust! When patients feel heard, they are much more willing to listen to your medical guidance. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T4#GNS311_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why is folic acid so important before and during early pregnancy?

options.A: To prevent neural tube defects
options.B: To strengthen the mother's bones
options.C: To lower maternal blood pressure
options.D: To stop excessive morning sickness

question: Why is teamwork and good communication so great for patients?

question: What are the three core elements of a true experimental study?

options.A: Blinding, placebo, and sampling

question: Why must nurses learn about different cultural and spiritual beliefs surrounding death?

options.C: To ensure every family follows the exact same hospital protocol

explanation: Cultural safety means honoring traditions and spiritual needs without letting personal judgments get in the way of great care. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T10#GNS321_U4_T10_h7)

question: Which lifestyle habit is crucial to screen for because it directly harms a developing baby during pregnancy?

question: A mother brings her healthy six-month-old baby to the clinic. What services should she get today?

question: Why must you always wash a dirty instrument thoroughly before applying a liquid chemical disinfectant?

options.D: Cleaning chemicals neutralize the toxic residue left behind by previous sterilisation cycles

question: Which group of medications is commonly used as a short-term fix to manage annoying bleeding caused by progestin implants?

question: Why does a toddler often need a higher weight-based drug dose than an infant?

question: Why do community nurses still use paper records and stationery instead of computers all the time?

question: A postpartum mum complains of calf pain and swelling in one leg. What serious condition should you suspect first?

question: How are benign tumors different from malignant ones?

question: Which of the following describes the main characteristic feature of pertussis infection?

question: What is the very first thing you must do when starting a counselling session with a patient?

question: A family caregiver looks totally exhausted and says they can't handle daily wound care anymore. What should you do first?

question: What is the single most effective way to stop the spread of hospital infections?

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when a patient arrives with sudden, severe breathlessness?

question: Which white blood cells are mainly responsible for making antibodies?

question: How does heavy data scatter (noise) inside your groups affect your final t-score?

question: Which of these is NOT an ethical concern when using health wearables?

question: Why does intravenous therapy carry a higher risk of severe adverse reactions compared to oral medications?

question: Which part of a child's bone allows it to grow longer as they get older?

question: Why do we use a clean razor blade from a birth kit to cut the baby's cord?

question: Why is an oral dose of an opioid usually higher than its intravenous (IV) dose?

question: A nurse walks into a room and notices a patient clutching their chest and breathing heavily. What category of the general survey does this fall under?

question: Which of these actions is an example of professional negligence?

question: What is a common social double standard regarding the sexuality of adolescent boys and girls?

question: Which specific mineral ion is mainly responsible for making things taste salty?

question: A client on combined oral contraceptive pills reports getting severe migraine headaches with visual changes (auras) lately. What should you do first?

question: When assessing a postpartum mother at home, what does a firm uterine fundus indicate?

question: Why is good communication among home health team members so vital?

question: What happens right in the center of an old TB tubercle as the infection sits there?

question: How do nurse-led community outreach programs help improve maternal health in rural Nigeria?

question: A patient with a blood pressure of 220/130 mmHg complains of a sudden, blinding headache and confusion. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

question: Why is the immediate postpartum period considered the most critical time for postnatal care checks?

question: Which of these traits tells us that a material is hazardous waste?

question: A patient wants to bake a healthier cake with less refined sugar. What is a great nursing suggestion?

question: Why does the intestinal wall have a muscular layer (the muscularis)?

question: A patient is discouraged because their BMI hasn't budged after starting an exercise routine. What else can you suggest tracking?
